facts.raw_span: A 68-year-old man
pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
underwent Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty (DSAEK) in the right eye
history of an eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa (pine processionary) 9 months before DSAEK
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
no pain with ocular movements
brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
no conjunctival hyperemia, no discharge, and no epithelial defect
The anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography of the right eye revealed a central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma

concepts.why: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on anterior segment optical coherence tomography suggest fungal keratitis.
The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the absence of conjunctival hyperemia, discharge, and epithelial defect suggest bacterial keratitis.
The history of Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty (DSAEK) and the decreased best-corrected visual acuity suggest corneal graft rejection.

The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on anterior segment optical coherence tomography suggest Acanthamoeba keratitis.
The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the absence of conjunctival hyperemia, discharge, and epithelial defect suggest Herpes simplex keratitis.
The history of Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty (DSAEK) and the decreased best-corrected visual acuity suggest postoperative keratitis.

The history of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa (pine processionary) and the presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma suggest Thaumetopoea pityocampa keratitis.
The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma and the absence of conjunctival hyperemia, discharge, and epithelial defect suggest corneal ulcer.

rationales.F03: The patient underwent DSAEK, which increases the risk of corneal graft rejection and postoperative keratitis.
rationales.F04: The patient had a history of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa, which increases the risk of Thaumetopoea pityocampa keratitis.
rationales.F08: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma is suggestive of fungal keratitis.
rationales.F12: The anterior segment optical coherence tomography revealed a central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma, which is consistent with postoperative keratitis and fungal keratitis.

no clear evidence of graft rejection
